data.question: Is this really free?
data.answer: Yes. Completely free, no credit card required. It is the PDF version of a guide I published on my blog, packaged so you can read it offline and keep it.

data.question: What format is the guide?
data.answer: A **62-page PDF** with a table of contents and clickable links. The living version is also published on [dsebastien.net](https://www.dsebastien.net/the-complete-guide-to-obsidian-automation/) and is updated as the tooling evolves.

data.question: I am new to Obsidian. Should I start here?
data.answer: Not yet. Start with the free [Beginner's Guide to Obsidian](/product/beginners-guide-obsidian), get a working vault, then come back to automation.

data.question: Do I need to be a developer?
data.answer: No for Layer 1 (everything inside `Obsidian`). Layer 2 and 3 get more technical (command line, `Git`, MCP, AI agents), and the guide explains each concept before using it.

data.question: Which plugins does it cover?
data.answer: `Templater`, `QuickAdd`, `Dataview`, `Bases`, `Linter`, `Meta Bind`, `Commander`, `Auto Note Mover`, `Obsidian Git`, `Local REST API`, MCP servers, and many more, always tied to the job they do rather than as a list.

data.question: Does it cover AI agents on the vault?
data.answer: Yes, the whole of Layer 3: instruction files, skills, hooks, MCP, multi-agent workflows, scheduled agents, vault maintenance that runs itself, and the risks (including how to keep AI out of your vault when you want to).

data.question: I want all of this pre-built. Is there a shortcut?
data.answer: That is exactly what the [Obsidian Starter Kit](/product/obsidian-starter-kit) is: the vault structure, note types, templates, automations, and the AI skills library from the guide, ready to use.
